answer: The Bell circuit ran on the real sirius QPU with 100 shots. The job ID is 01a15f16-b72f-701e-8638-31fba83e0ec7. The counts were 00: 56, 01: 2, 10: 3, and 11: 39. Both bits agreed in 95 of 100 shots, which is a fraction of 0.95. Before the paid run, I ran the same circuit once on the free sirius:mock alias to test the script. That test job was 01a15f16-8e40-7634-931b-214afff5eea7 and returned 00: 100. Only one real job was submitted, so only one job spent credits. The script is at /Users/claytonchancey/Desktop/quantum/.claude/worktrees/wf_1a6926f8-f6c-1/scratch/bell.py. It reads IQM_TOKEN from the .env file through the environment, because iqm-client raises an error if the token is passed both as an argument and as an environment variable.
